title: DMM-1 — Data Model Maps Foundation Delivery
summary: inventory current data authorities, prove a readable mapping notation, and publish the first durable logical and projection maps
content_html:
DMM-1 — Data Model Maps Foundation Delivery

Status And Purpose

In progress at the DMM-1.0 checkpoint. Data Model Maps Concept And Examples defines the mixed logical ERD, projection-lineage, and artefact-register approach tested by this delivery. DMM-1.1 has not started.

The delivery creates the first durable, reviewable orientation layer for current canonical entities and generated projections. It begins with a bounded notation and readability spike because Mermaid syntax support is already proven, while large-diagram legibility and correct partitioning remain the material risks.

Complete Outcome

One durable Data Model Maps index under the existing Architecture documentation routes to three bounded current-state maps:

  1. Catalogue logical model and read-model boundary.
  2. Docs Viewer main-scope, sub-scope, manage, search, and public projection lineage.
  3. Cross-system relationship projections for Semantic Tokens, Tags, Project State, and Resolver Tokens, with proposed relationships labelled separately from shipped ones.

Each map combines only the diagram types it needs with a concise artefact register naming exact source, producer, primary consumers, visibility, refresh behavior, and code/config/test authority. A reader can follow a canonical record into its relevant projections without mistaking generated files for canonical entities.

Delivery Discipline

DMM-1 is documentation-only. It reuses fenced Mermaid and Diagram Detail View in Studio Docs Viewer and does not add production runtime, schemas, builders, registries, or UI.

DMM-1.0 must inventory the exact proposed document paths, mapped code/config/test owners, and expected documentation diff before the full map set is approved. The likely production and test diff is zero. If useful completion requires a generator, parser, schema registry, new lint target, or runtime interaction, stop and propose a separate delivery rather than widening DMM-1.

DMM-1.0 Checkpoint Record

Product Emphasis

The durable result is a small set of useful system explanations, not an index of every diagram. Feature specifications may use the same notation for paired current before and explicitly proposed after diagrams. Retained maps should be reviewed after major deliveries that change a displayed relationship; DMM-1 does not promise continuous diagram drift maintenance.

Authority Inventory

Catalogue

  • Canonical: studio/data/canonical/catalogue/works.json, series.json, work_details/<work_id>.json, and optional catalogue-markdown/{works,series}/<id>.md. studio/services/catalogue/catalogue_source.py owns record loading, normalization, validation, and serialization; write services and transactions own accepted mutations.
  • Generated public: site/assets/data/{series_index,works_index,recent_index}.json, site/assets/{series,works}/index/<id>.json, and site/assets/data/search/catalogue/index.json. catalogue_generation_*.py, generate_work_pages.py, and search/build_search.py produce them through the scoped build selected after canonical mutation or an explicit build.
  • Generated Studio: studio/data/generated/catalogue-lookup/{work_search,series_search}.json and series/<series_id>.json. catalogue_lookup.py and catalogue_lookup_refresh.py own full or field-planned targeted refresh. Focused Work/detail read payloads are runtime-only service projections and are not another stored canonical family.
  • Focused evidence: test_catalogue_source_mutation.py, test_catalogue_generation_{indexes,writes}.py, and test_catalogue_lookup_refresh.py. Catalogue Source Model and Catalogue Indexes And Payloads remain the durable contract routers.

Docs Viewer

  • Authored: docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/source/documents/<doc_id>.md plus configured source/sub-scopes/<sub_scope>/documents/<doc_id>.md. docs_scopes.json owns scope type, storage, viewer route, sub-scopes, and public-projection destinations.
  • Generated working main scope: published/documents/{index-tree.json,recent.json,by-id/<doc_id>.json,semantic-tokens/index.json} from DocsDataBuilder; published/search/index.json is independently produced by build_search.py. Full builds refresh the family; targeted builds replace selected by-ID and usage rows while recalculating the small navigation/Recent projections.
  • Generated working sub-scope: published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub_scope>/{manifest.json,manage-manifest.json,by-id/<doc_id>.json} from SubScopeDocsBuilder. The public-safe manifest omits hidden and management fields; the manage manifest retains management rows and registered customisation. Sub-scope documents remain outside the parent Index, Recent, and search.
  • Explicit public publication: configured public scopes are copied only through docs_publish_gate.py to site/assets/data/docs/scopes/<scope>/ and site/assets/data/search/<scope>/index.json; publishable sub-scope projections include manifest.json and by-ID payloads, never manage-manifest.json. Runtime readers consume the projection selected by route and access mode.
  • Focused evidence: test_build_docs_payloads.py, test_build_docs_subscopes.py, test_build_search_python.py, test_build_docs_public_payloads.py, and test_docs_publish_gate.py. Generated Data Contracts, Projection Contract, and docs_scopes.json remain the current owners.

Cross-System Relationships

  • Shipped Semantic Tokens: canonical Catalogue records and the published Moments Docs projection feed docs-viewer/data/generated/semantic-tokens/target-lookup.json through SemanticTargetLookupBuilder. A scope Docs build consumes that management lookup while rendering tokens and replaces its generated semantic-tokens/index.json; target refresh and document rebuild are separate. test_semantic_target_lookup.py and the semantic-token catalogue tests own focused evidence.
  • Shipped Tag document associations: studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json (tag_registry_v5) owns ordered doc_url[]; tag_source_model.py, registry mutation services, and transaction services own writes. Public document-locations.json projections are separately built from already-published Docs search, parent payloads, and sub-scope manifests for the Tag picker; they are not Tag authority. test_tag_source_model.py, test_tag_registry_mutations.py, and test_build_document_locations.py are the focused evidence.
  • Proposed only: Tag Semantic Tokens, the new folder-centred Project State generation, and Resolver Tokens have architecture documents but no shipped lookup, parser, renderer, or relationship projection. Their nodes and edges must be labelled proposed. The existing var/studio/reports/project-state.md image-audit output is a different shipped workflow and is intentionally excluded from the proposed relationship map.

Mapping Language And Partitions

  • ERDs contain logical identity and cardinality only. Array-backed references may be shown as logical foreign keys, but files, builders, indexes, and access modes do not become entities.
  • Lineage diagrams contain physical reads, builds, publication, and consumption. Every artefact node carries one of canonical, authored, generated projection, or runtime-only; arrows use an explicit verb where direction alone could be ambiguous.
  • Registers carry exact path or path family, producer, primary consumer, refresh trigger, visibility, and code/config/test authority. Operational detail does not migrate into diagram labels merely to make the register shorter.
  • Shipped edges are solid. Proposed nodes say proposed in their label and use dashed edges inside a visibly separate proposed section. A proposal does not enter a current-state diagram merely because planning exists.
  • A feature-spec before/after pair reuses stable node names. Before is verified current state; after — proposed is a design claim until delivery updates the current map.
  • The Catalogue map uses one logical ERD plus one small read-model boundary flow. The Docs Viewer map is split into main working projections, sub-scope projections, and explicit public publication. The cross-system document contains separate mini-lineages for Semantic Tokens, Tags, and proposed Project State/Resolver behavior. No master graph is created.

Readability Spike

The representative concept diagrams rendered successfully in managed Studio with pinned Mermaid 11.16.0, accessibility titles/descriptions, graphics-document roles, and no Mermaid warnings. In the ordinary layout, the Catalogue ERD rendered at 238 × 308 inside a 560-pixel host and the Docs lineage at 530 × 554. At a 390 × 844 narrow viewport, they rendered at 238 × 308 and 324 × 339 inside a 354-pixel host without clipping. The lineage remains readable but is at the acceptable density ceiling, which supports the three-way Docs partition above.

Both rendered diagrams expose Open diagram in new tab controls and stable SVG viewBox metadata. The automated browser was prevented from following the Blob detail target by its navigation security policy, so manual Diagram Detail visual review remains the one open DMM-1.0 evidence item; this is not a product failure.

Exact DMM-1.1 Documentation Shape

  • Promote d-20260802-123451-d0e52e.md into the concise durable Data Model Maps index beneath Architecture; do not create another diagram catalogue.
  • Create d-20260802-205910-533be0.md — Catalogue Data Model Map.
  • Create d-20260802-205911-bec41f.md — Docs Viewer Projection Map.
  • Create d-20260802-205912-16bc10.md — Cross-System Relationship Map.
  • Add one inbound link to d-20260331-000000-4a16b0.md (Architecture) and keep planning/closeout links in the feature parent and this delivery until explicit retirement approval.

Expected DMM-1.1 authored diff is roughly 320–430 lines across the promoted index, three new map documents, Architecture link, and delivery/parent status updates. Production files: none. Test files: none. Canonical data, application payloads, and public site behavior: unchanged. Existing builders will regenerate only the affected Studio Docs by-ID/tree/Recent/search projections.

Rough Delivery Steps

DMM-1.0 — Inventory And Freeze The Mapping Language

  • [x] Inventory the current canonical, authored, generated, runtime-only, manage-only, and public artefact families needed by the three proposed maps.
  • [x] Trace exact producers, primary consumers, refresh triggers, visibility boundaries, and existing durable owners from current code, configuration, schemas, and focused tests.
  • [x] Freeze the distinction between logical entity relationships, physical derivation/publication edges, and register-only operational detail.
  • [ ] Render representative Catalogue ERD and Docs Viewer lineage examples with the pinned Mermaid version in ordinary and narrow layouts, using Diagram Detail View for inspection. Ordinary and narrow rendering pass; manual Diagram Detail visual review remains.
  • [x] Decide the smallest readable partition for each map and record intentional omissions rather than creating one master diagram.
  • [x] Record the exact new or promoted document list, current links to update, and rough documentation diff. Record production and test files explicitly as none unless the reviewed shape changes.

Checkpoint: the reviewed spike can trace one Catalogue relationship and one main/sub-scope Docs Viewer source through their projections without ambiguous authority, crossed-edge reconstruction, unreadable labels, or unsupported Mermaid behavior. Stop before writing the complete inventory.

DMM-1.1 — Publish The Durable Map Set

  • [ ] Create or promote one concise durable Data Model Maps index beneath the existing Architecture documentation.
  • [ ] Publish the Catalogue logical model and its adjacent canonical/public/Studio artefact register.
  • [ ] Publish the Docs Viewer projection-lineage map and register, separating main scope, sub-scope, manage, search, and explicit public publication.
  • [ ] Publish the cross-system relationship-projection map and register, distinguishing shipped Catalogue Semantic Token projections and Tag Registry document associations from proposed Tag Semantic Token, Project State, and Resolver Token behavior.
  • [ ] Link each map to current implementation and contract owners without copying exhaustive schemas or code inventories into unrelated durable documents.
  • [ ] Add only the minimum inbound navigation needed from the Architecture index or an existing focused owner.

Checkpoint: every displayed entity and artefact has one unambiguous classification and owner; every generated edge identifies its producer; every access boundary and proposed relationship is explicit; omitted families are named.

DMM-1.2 — Verify, Review, And Transfer

  • [ ] Render every Mermaid block through the current Studio Docs Viewer runtime and inspect the ordinary document view plus Diagram Detail View.
  • [ ] Review wide and narrow presentation, long paths, edge crossings, labels, accessibility titles/descriptions, and source readability in a normal Markdown editor.
  • [ ] Verify all document and code-authority links, exact artefact paths, canonical/derived classifications, and shipped/proposed states against the current repository.
  • [ ] Rebuild the exact Docs documents and Studio search projection, run git diff --check, and perform a final source/diff/omission review.
  • [ ] Rewrite the retained concept as current durable orientation material if it remains the best owner; present the feature parent, concept, and delivery closeout list for explicit retirement or promotion approval.

Focused Evidence

  • the pinned Mermaid renderer accepts every maintained ERD and flowchart;
  • each diagram remains usable in the rendered document and Diagram Detail View at realistic density;
  • register paths and producer/consumer claims resolve to current repository owners;
  • Docs Viewer build and search projections contain the new hierarchy and rendered examples; and
  • final review confirms that no runtime, canonical data, generated application payload, or public site behavior changed.

Not In Scope

  • a whole-repository master ERD or unrestricted dependency graph;
  • field-by-field reproduction of every JSON or front-matter schema;
  • automatic Mermaid generation, source-code introspection, or a schema registry;
  • a graph database, query language, interactive explorer, filters, collapsing, or runtime traversal;
  • new projection, mutation, publication, refresh, or watcher behavior;
  • declaring authored documentation to be executable schema authority;
  • changing existing canonical or generated artefacts to make the diagrams simpler; or
  • mapping unrelated filesystem, code-import, CSS, or UI-component dependencies.

The Data Model Maps feature parent owns planning and navigation. At completion, Architecture should own the durable map entry point.
